name: ReorderableListView
summary: Flutter's `ReorderableListView`: a list whose items are reordered by dragging.
doc:
Flutter's `ReorderableListView`: a list whose items are reordered by
dragging.

```dart
ReorderableListView(
  onReorder: todo.reorder,        // void reorder(int oldIndex, int newIndex)
  children: [for (final t in tasks) TaskTile(key: ValueKey(t.id), task: t)],
)

// A list the browser changes (rows are cloned from a template):
Watch.list(
  todo.items,
  itemKey: todo.keyOf,
  container: (rows) => ReorderableListView(onReorder: todo.reorder, children: rows),
  each: (row) => TaskTile(task: row),
)
```

Each item gets a handle (a button with an icon, `buildDefaultDragHandles`)
and a finger held on the item drags it (a touch); the mouse drags by the
handle, or by a [ReorderableDragStartListener] you place. The dragged item
follows the pointer through a CSS `translate` and the others slide out of
the way with CSS transitions (no Dart per frame); the page scrolls when the
pointer is near its edge. On release the engine moves the item in the page
and calls [onReorder] (a method of a `ThorState`) with the indexes as Flutter
gives them: over a `Watch.list` the list finds its rows already in order.

Keyboard (WCAG 2.5.7 and 2.1.1: a drag needs another way): the handle is a
button. Space or Enter picks the item up, the arrow keys move it, Space or
Enter drops it (that calls [onReorder]), Escape puts it back; Alt+arrow
anywhere in an item moves it one place at once. A live region says each step
([labels] changes the words).

`// web:` Flutter's `proxyDecorator` has no equivalent ([draggingStyle]
is the dragged item's look); the per-frame callbacks and
`autoScrollerVelocityScalar` neither. One item is dragged at a time. Without
JavaScript the list is only its items. A state that does not apply a
reorder leaves the item where it was dropped until the list changes again.

name: ResponsiveLayout
summary: Different layouts per screen size — the web counterpart of switching on `MediaQuery.sizeOf(context).width` or `LayoutBuilder`.
doc:
Different layouts per screen size — the web counterpart of switching on
`MediaQuery.sizeOf(context).width` or `LayoutBuilder`.

**Every variant is rendered** and CSS shows the right one, so it works
with SSR and never flashes. The price: the hidden variants are in the
HTML too, so what is in both is sent, parsed and kept twice (a 24-product
grid in `mobile` and in `desktop` is a 24-product grid shipped twice, and
a `FutureBuilder` or a `Watch.list` in both is drawn and kept in sync
twice). Use it for chrome that really differs (a drawer against a top
bar), and keep what the variants have in common out of it.

When only the *arrangement* changes, prefer **one tree** with `.when()`:
the same widgets, another layout per breakpoint, nothing duplicated.

```dart
// WRONG: the grid is in the page twice
ResponsiveLayout(
  mobile: ProductGrid(columns: 2, products: products),
  desktop: ProductGrid(columns: 4, products: products),
)

// RIGHT: one grid, its columns per breakpoint
Grid(
  layout: GridLayout(columns: 2, gap: 8).when(expanded: GridLayout(columns: 4)),
  children: [for (final p in products) ProductCard(p)],
)

// RIGHT: a column that becomes a row from `lg`
Column(
  layout: FlexLayout().when(expanded: FlexLayout(direction: Axis.horizontal)),
  children: [sidebar, Expanded(child: content)],
)
```

`thor dev` warns (THOR-R034) when two variants both carry a
`FutureBuilder`, both a `Watch.list`, or both more than 16 KB of HTML.

name: Scaffold
summary: Flutter's `Scaffold`, as a semantic page grid: `header` (appBar) / `main` (body) / `footer` (bottomNavigationBar), at least one viewport tall (`100dvh`, correct on mobile browsers).
doc:
Flutter's `Scaffold`, as a semantic page grid:
`header` (appBar) / `main` (body) / `footer` (bottomNavigationBar),
at least one viewport tall (`100dvh`, correct on mobile browsers).

A [drawer] (or [endDrawer]) is a native modal `<dialog>` the [AppBar]
opens with a menu button it adds by itself (see `DrawerButton`); no JS.
A `Drawer(permanentFrom:)` there is the same panel from that breakpoint
up, beside the body under the bars (the menu button goes away).

It starts with a skip link (the first Tab stop: "Skip to content", shown
only while it has the focus) to its `<main>`; [skipLink] turns it off.

```dart
Scaffold(
  appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Sales')),
  body: ListView(children: rows),
  floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(onPressed: add, child: Icon(plus)),
  floatingActionButtonLocation: FloatingActionButtonLocation.centerDocked,
  bottomNavigationBar: NavigationBar(destinations: tabs),
)
```

With a `CustomScrollView` as the [body] the body scrolls inside the
scaffold (the bars stay where they are), as in Flutter: the scaffold is
then exactly one viewport tall.

name: SegmentedButton
summary: Flutter's `SegmentedButton<T>`: a row of [segments] to choose one value (or several) from.
doc:
Flutter's `SegmentedButton<T>`: a row of [segments] to choose one value
(or several) from.

```dart
SegmentedButton<View>(
  segments: const [
    ButtonSegment(value: View.list, label: Text('List')),
    ButtonSegment(value: View.grid, label: Text('Grid')),
  ],
  selected: const {View.list},
  onSelectionChanged: browse.setView, // a ThorState method taking Set<View>
)
```

Like Flutter: [selected] is the chosen values, [onSelectionChanged]
receives the set the person picks, and `onSelectionChanged: null`
disables the control.

`// web:` the segments are native inputs (no JavaScript needed to choose):
a radio group, or checkboxes with [multiSelectionEnabled]. The keys
(arrow keys in a radio group, Space in checkboxes), focus, form value and
screen reader names are the browser's. A radio cannot be unchecked, so
[emptySelectionAllowed] only means that [selected] may start empty, and
with [multiSelectionEnabled] the last checked segment can still be
unchecked. Because the browser holds the choice, [selected] is the value
the page is drawn with; the state's handler receives the new set when
the person picks (for a radio group the browser sends one value, for
checkboxes all the checked ones). A control with no `onSelectionChanged`
argument at all is not disabled: the browser keeps the choice and the
page's CSS reads it.

`// web:` Flutter's `ButtonStyle` holds `WidgetStateProperty`s; here
[style] is the look of every segment and [selectedStyle] the look of a
chosen one.

params.doc: The accessible name announced by assistive technology (`aria-label`).

params.name: image

params.name: hidden

params.name: rowCount

params.name: columnIndex

params.name: value

params.doc: What happens when [child] is used, read after its name (`aria-description`).

params.name: checked

params.name: expanded

params.name: readOnly

params.name: obscured
params.doc: Whether [child] hides its text, like a password.

params.name: focusable

params.name: textField
params.doc: Announces [child] as a text field (`role="textbox"`).

params.name: slider
params.doc: Announces [child] as a slider (`role="slider"`; its value is the [value] text, and `aria-valuenow` too when it is a number: give it one).

params.name: container
params.doc: Groups [child]'s content into one node (`role="group"` when [child] has no role of its own: never over a button or a list item).

params.name: explicitChildNodes
params.doc: Whether the children of [child] are separate nodes.

params.name: excludeSemantics
params.doc: Replaces what [child]'s content says with this node alone (Flutter's `excludeSemantics`).

params.name: sortKey
params.doc: The order assistive technology reads [child] in among its siblings.

name: ShareRequest
summary: Opens the device's share sheet when its child is tapped.
doc:
Opens the device's share sheet when its child is tapped.

```dart
ShareRequest(
  title: 'Tacos El Güero',
  text: 'The best tacos in town',
  url: '/places/tacos-el-guero',
  onResult: place.shared, // void shared(String result)
  child: const Link(href: 'https://wa.me/?text=...', child: Text('Share')),
)
```

`// web:` Flutter's `share_plus` shares from Dart; here the tap calls the
browser's `navigator.share`, which needs a tap and a secure page, and
exists on phones and a few desktops. Where it does not, a child that is a
link keeps its own `href` (the page's fallback, also what it does without
JavaScript: a `wa.me` or `mailto:` link); a child with no link copies the
text and the link to the clipboard. [onResult] says what happened:
`shared`, `cancelled` (the visitor closed the sheet), `link` (the child's
link was followed), `copied` or `failed`, so a state can show "Link
copied". [url] may be a path; without it the current page is shared.

name: Shortcuts
summary: Flutter's `Shortcuts`: key presses inside [child] (while the focus is in it) become [Intent]s, and the nearest [Actions] around the focus that has an action for the intent's type runs it.
doc:
Flutter's `Shortcuts`: key presses inside [child] (while the focus is in
it) become [Intent]s, and the nearest [Actions] around the focus that has
an action for the intent's type runs it.

```dart
class SaveIntent extends Intent {
  const SaveIntent();
}

Shortcuts(
  shortcuts: const {
    SingleActivator(LogicalKeyboardKey.keyS, meta: true): SaveIntent(),
  },
  child: Actions(
    actions: {SaveIntent: CallbackAction<SaveIntent>(onInvoke: editor.save)},
    child: Focus(child: form),
  ),
)
// void save(SaveIntent intent) { … }   (in EditorViewModel)
```

Like in Flutter, the `Shortcuts` nearest the focus that has a matching
activator decides the intent; with no action for it the key goes on to
the outer shortcuts. The keys a text field edits with stay in it, and
with nothing focused the outermost shortcuts on view answer, as with
[CallbackShortcuts].

`// web:` decorates [child]'s element instead of adding a node (with a
[CallbackShortcuts] or a `Focus(onKeyEvent:)` on the same element,
`onKeyEvent` goes first, then these, then the callbacks). Intents are
known by their class name.

child's size that shows along [axis], clipped, with the child aligned by

```dart

  sizeFactor: CurvedAnimation(parent: panel.open, curve: Curves.easeOut),
  axisAlignment: -1,
  child: Details(item),
```

render, `onVisible`). The size is a grid track of `<n>fr` (Radix's
collapsible measures the height in JS; `interpolate-size: allow-keywords`

name: Skeleton
summary: A placeholder for content that is still loading: a rounded box with a light that sweeps across it (the look of `skeletonizer` and `shimmer`).
doc:
A placeholder for content that is still loading: a rounded box with a
light that sweeps across it (the look of `skeletonizer` and `shimmer`).

Draw it where the data will go, for the snapshot with no data of a
`FutureBuilder`: the page goes out with it at once, and the real content
takes its place when the future is done.

```dart
FutureBuilder<List<Product>>(
  future: data.featured,
  builder: (context, snapshot) => snapshot.hasData
      ? ProductGrid(snapshot.data!)
      : const Skeleton(height: 240),
)
```

To fill a parent that has a size (an `AspectRatio`), use
`Skeleton.expand()` (or `height: double.infinity`): the default is 16
high.
With a nullable type (`Future<Product?>`) check `snapshot.connectionState
!= ConnectionState.done` for the skeleton: `hasData` is also `false` for a
future that completed with `null`, which would keep it for good.

`// web:` the animation is CSS (a gradient that moves, nothing runs in the
browser's code) and stops with `prefers-reduced-motion`. It is hidden from
assistive technology (`aria-hidden`) and, without JavaScript, from the
page: the content that replaces it is shown at the end of the page then.

name: SplitPane
summary: Two panes with a draggable divider between them: the editors' split view.
doc:
Two panes with a draggable divider between them: the editors' split view.

```dart
SplitPane(
  initialFraction: 0.3,
  minFirstSize: 160,
  minSecondSize: 320,
  semanticLabel: 'Resize the sidebar',
  first: const Sidebar(),
  second: const Canvas(),
)
```

[axis] is Flutter's `Row` / `Column` direction: [Axis.horizontal] puts
[first] on the start side and [second] on the end side (a vertical
divider), [Axis.vertical] stacks them. The size of [first] is
`initialFraction` of the room left by the divider, kept between
[minFirstSize] and the room that leaves [minSecondSize] to [second]: that
is CSS (`clamp()` on a custom property), so the first paint is right, the
bounds hold when the window resizes and the page works with no JS.

The divider is a focusable `role="separator"` (the WAI-ARIA window
splitter) with `aria-valuenow` as the percent given to [first]. With the
lite engine it moves: the arrows resize by 2 % (10 % with Shift), Home and
End go to the smallest and the largest [first], and a pointer drags it.

`// web:` Flutter has no split view (an app writes a `Row` of two
`Expanded` and a `GestureDetector`, and keeps the fraction in a
`State`); the divider is one more element of the page, and the browser
holds the fraction: it is not a field of a `ThorState`. [onChanged] tells
a state method the fraction (0 to 1) *after* each interaction (the end of
a drag, a key press), not on every pixel of the drag, so the state can
persist it.

Flutter's `TabBar` (Material 3 primary tabs), with no JS: each tab is a
`<label>` around a visually hidden radio of the `DefaultTabController`'s
group. Arrow keys move the selection natively; the checked tab shows
the indicator and its `TabBarView` panel (`:has()`).

```dart
DefaultTabController(
  id: 'order',
  length: 2,
  child: Column(children: [
    const TabBar(tabs: [Tab(text: 'Details'), Tab(text: 'Payments')]),
    const TabBarView(children: [Text('…'), Text('…')]),
  ]),
)
```

`// web:` the indicator spans the whole tab (`TabBarIndicatorSize.tab`)
and doesn't slide between tabs; the selection is exposed as a radio
group until the engine loads, then as tabs.

underlined with the text, since the indicator is a shadow the browser
drops.

summary: Flutter's `TextField` → a native `<input>` inside a decorated row.
doc:
Flutter's `TextField` → a native `<input>` inside a decorated row.

Layout follows Flutter's InputDecorator (Material 3): a prefix/suffix
icon sits in a 48×48 box, and when present it replaces the start/end
content padding (with a 4px gap). The focused border is applied with
`:focus-within`, so focus styling needs no Dart state.

With a `labelText`, `helperText` or `errorText` the row sits in a
column: the label above (a `<label for>` the control), the helper or
error line below (the control's `aria-describedby`; an error also sets
`aria-invalid`). `// web:` the label sits above the border instead of
floating inside it. The control's id is [id], else `f-<name>`, else one
unique in the page.

  String? datalist,
  String obscuringCharacter = '\u2022',

})

params.name: decoration
params.doc: The visual properties (label, icons, border…) around the input.

params.name: style
params.doc: The style to apply to the input's text.

params.name: keyboardType
params.doc: The keyboard/`<input type>` to use for text entry. Null is [TextInputType.text].

params.name: obscureText
params.doc: Whether to hide the text being edited (`<input type="password">`).

params.name: maxLines
params.doc: Visible lines: more than 1 makes a multi-line `<textarea>` with that many rows (Flutter: `maxLines`). Null grows without limit (from [minLines], 1 by default). `// web:` without [minLines] a number keeps that height and scrolls instead of growing up to `maxLines`; null and [minLines] grow with CSS `field-sizing: content` (a browser without it keeps the starting rows and scrolls).

params.name: minLines
params.doc: Lines shown when the field is empty (Flutter: `minLines`, at most [maxLines]): a `<textarea>` that starts that tall and grows with its text up to [maxLines]. `// web:` it grows with CSS `field-sizing`; browsers without it keep [minLines] rows and scroll.

params.name: enabled
params.doc: Whether the field accepts input. Null is enabled.

params.name: autofocus
params.doc: Whether to focus the field automatically when it is first shown.

params.name: name
params.doc: Form field name.

params.name: initialValue
params.doc: The text to prefill the field with.

params.name: controller
params.doc: A `TextEditingController` field of a `ThorState`: the field shows its text (over [initialValue]) and typing updates it.

params.name: focusNode
params.doc: A `FocusNode` field of a `ThorState` that focuses this field from a method (`node.requestFocus()`).

params.name: onChanged
params.doc: Called with the current value on every keystroke (`input` event).

params.name: onSubmitted
params.doc: Called with the current value when the field is submitted (Enter key). `// web:` with a `ThorState` method, Enter doesn't submit the enclosing form (it runs the method instead).

params.name: clearOnSubmitted
params.doc: Empty the field after [onSubmitted] (a tag or chat input).

params.name: id
params.doc: DOM id of the `<input>`.

params.name: inputAttributes
params.doc: More attributes for the `<input>` (validation, autocomplete…).

params.name: readOnly
params.doc: Whether the text can't be edited (`readonly`): it can still be focused, selected and copied, and it is sent with a form (unlike [enabled]).

params.name: maxLength
params.doc: The most characters the field takes, counted as Flutter counts them: user-perceived characters (grapheme clusters), so an emoji is one. A counter (`0/20`, live) shows below the field unless [InputDecoration.counterText] is `''`; [noMaxLength] counts without limiting.

params.name: textInputAction
params.doc: The enter key of the virtual keyboard (`enterkeyhint`). web: a keyboard hint only: the enter key still submits the form (or runs `onSubmitted`).

params.name: textCapitalization
params.doc: How the virtual keyboard capitalizes (`autocapitalize`). Left null the browser decides (Flutter's `none` is `TextCapitalization.none`, which sets `autocapitalize="off"`).

params.name: textAlign
params.doc: How the text aligns inside the field (`text-align`).

params.name: autofillHints
params.doc: What the field holds, for the browser to autofill it (`autocomplete`): [AutofillHints] names or HTML tokens. Under [inputAttributes].

params.name: datalist
params.doc: The id of a `Datalist` whose options the browser suggests while typing (`list`). Under [inputAttributes].

params.name: obscuringCharacter
params.doc: Flutter's character that hides a password. web: the browser draws its own dots in `<input type="password">`; this is accepted and not used.

params.name: expands
params.doc: Whether the field fills the height its parent gives it (a `<textarea>` with no rows; put it in an `Expanded` or a sized box, as in Flutter). [minLines] must be null.

name: ThorApp
summary: Root of a thor app, like `MaterialApp`: turns widget styles into deduplicated, conditional stylesheets instead of inline `style` attributes.
doc:
Root of a thor app, like `MaterialApp`: turns widget styles into
deduplicated, conditional stylesheets instead of inline `style` attributes.

On the server the collected rules are written into `<head>` once the tree
is built; in the browser new rules are inserted at runtime. Without a
ThorApp, widgets fall back to inline styles (and local `<style>` tags for
conditional rules), so everything still works, just less compactly.

summary: Flutter's `Tooltip`: a bubble with [message] (or [richMessage]) that shows while the pointer is over [child] or it has keyboard focus, with no JS.
doc:
Flutter's `Tooltip`: a bubble with [message] (or [richMessage]) that
shows while the pointer is over [child] or it has keyboard focus, with
no JS.

web: the bubble is the element right after the child's, shown by CSS
(`:hover`/`:focus-visible` of the child, after [waitDuration]) and
placed by anchor positioning below the child ([preferBelow]), flipping
to the other side when it doesn't fit. Both sit in a box that takes no
part in the layout (`display: contents`) and scopes the anchor. The
child points at the bubble with `aria-describedby`. Unlike Flutter: no
long press on touch (a tap that focuses a control shows it), no Esc to
dismiss it, and a browser without anchor positioning shows the bubble
where it would sit in the page, next to the child.

As the state of a `Watch` the box is the state's element (it carries the
state mark and the other states are its siblings, like any widget that
renders more than one element).

name: TweenAnimationBuilder
summary: Flutter's `TweenAnimationBuilder`: builds [builder] with the tween's target and animates the change when the target changes.
doc:
Flutter's `TweenAnimationBuilder`: builds [builder] with the tween's
target and animates the change when the target changes.

```dart
Watch(card.hovered, builder: (hovered) => TweenAnimationBuilder<double>(
  tween: Tween(end: hovered ? 1.0 : 0.0),
  duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 200),
  builder: (context, lift, child) => Transform.translate(
    offset: Offset(0, -8 * lift),
    child: child,
  ),
  child: const Text('Card'),
))
```

`// web:` Flutter calls [builder] on every frame with the interpolated
value; here no Dart runs per frame. [builder] runs once per state with
`tween.end`, and the element it returns **transitions** (`transition:
all`) from the previous state's values to the new ones in CSS: opacity,
transform, colors, size, spacing, radius, shadows and any other
property CSS can interpolate. So:

- What animates is the root element of what [builder] returns (and the
  wrappers fused into it, like `Opacity` or `Transform`); changes to
  descendants don't animate unless they are `Animated*` widgets
  themselves.
- The value the builder receives is the target, never an intermediate
  one: don't use it to branch (`value > 0.5 ? a : b`) or to build
  different structures; that is a switch, not an animation
  (`AnimatedSwitcher`, `AnimatedCrossFade`).
- `tween.begin` is ignored: the first render shows the target (there is
  no entrance animation); the animation runs when a `Watch` swaps the
  state, from where the element is, like Flutter's retargeting.
- [onEnd] runs once per change in the browser when it is a `ThorState`
  method; honors `prefers-reduced-motion` (the change is instant).

For one value across many elements, put it in a CSS variable with an
`@property` and let the descendants read it; for the properties of one
element prefer the specific `Animated*` widget.

Flutter's `ValueListenableBuilder` on a field of a [ThorState]: a
[Watch]. The server renders the builder once per value (`bool` or enum
fields) and the browser shows the one that matches, like any `Watch`.

```dart
ValueListenableBuilder<bool>(
  valueListenable: panel.open,   // final open = state(false);
  builder: (context, open, child) => Text(open ? 'Open' : 'Closed'),
)
```

`// web:` the builder runs on the server only, once per value: what
changes must come from the `value` it receives. An `int` or a `String`
field has unbounded values, so it can't be prerendered (THOR-S013): show a
String with `Watch(state.field)`, an int with `Watch(state.field.call,
count: n, …)`. A [ValueListenable] that is not a `StateSignal` (a plain
`ValueNotifier`) is drawn once with its current value: nothing in the
browser listens to it (a `ThorState` field of that type is a build
error).

name: VisibilityDetector
summary: Reports when its child enters or leaves the viewport: an infinite list's "load more" sentinel, a reveal-on-scroll, a view counter.
doc:
Reports when its child enters or leaves the viewport: an infinite list's
"load more" sentinel, a reveal-on-scroll, a view counter.

```dart
// a ViewModel method: void seen(bool visible) { if (visible) loadMore(); }
VisibilityDetector(
  onVisibilityChanged: feed.seen,
  margin: 400, // starts 400 px before it shows
  child: const SizedBox(height: 1),
)
```

Without JavaScript nothing is reported, so the child is also the page's
way without it: a "Load more" link (`?cursor=`) the same list answers.

`// web:` Flutter has no such widget (the `visibility_detector` package
is the nearest, and reports a `VisibilityInfo`); here the browser's
`IntersectionObserver` calls a method of a `ThorState` with `true` or
`false`. It reports changes: an element that starts out of view says
nothing until it shows, and one that shows says `true` once (until it
leaves and comes back), so a sentinel that stays in view after its rows
loaded is not reported again; remove it (`if (hasMore)`) or let the next
rows push it away. The engine starts when the first change is reported.

constructors.name: VisibilityDetector
constructors.signature:
VisibilityDetector({
  Key? key,
  required void Function(bool) onVisibilityChanged,
  double threshold = 0,
  double margin = 0,
  bool once = false,
  required Widget child,
})
constructors.summary: Wraps [child], reporting to [onVisibilityChanged].

params.name: onVisibilityChanged
params.doc: Called with `true` when [child] shows and `false` when it stops showing: a method of a `ThorState` that takes a `bool`.

params.name: threshold
params.doc: The share of [child] that must show to count (0: one pixel; 1: all).

params.name: margin
params.doc: Logical pixels around the viewport that count as showing: `400` reports 400 px before the child scrolls into view.

params.name: once
params.doc: Reports only the first appearance (`true` once) and stops watching.

name: Watch
summary: The part of a page that changes in the browser, bound to a field or a method of a [ThorState]:
doc:
The part of a page that changes in the browser, bound to a field or a
method of a [ThorState]:

```dart
Watch(counter.label)                       // a text: source returns a String
Watch(counter.isZero, builder: (zero) =>   // states: bool, enum, or int with
    TextButton(onPressed: zero ? null : counter.reset, child: …))  // count
Watch.field(toast.visible, builder: (visible) =>   // a `state(false)` field
    SnackBar(visible: visible, content: …))        // (visible is a bool)
Watch.list(cart.lines,                     // a list: source returns a List
    itemKey: cart.lineKey,                 // row.key has its type
    each: (row) => Row(children: [row.text(cart.lineName), …]))
```

The server renders the current value (every state, for a finite
source); the browser only updates what changed. [builder] and the rows of [Watch.list]
run on the server only, so they can build any widget, but what they show
that changes must come from the state (the source, `row.text`).

constructors.name: Watch
constructors.signature:
Watch(
  T Function() source, {
  Key? key,
  Widget Function(T)? builder,
  int? count,
  TextStyle? style,
})
constructors.summary: Watches [source]: a method torn off from a ThorState (`counter.label`, `cart.isSelected.withArg(i)`) or a reactive field (`counter.count`). With a [builder] use [Watch.field] for a field: passed here as is, the compiler infers `Object?` for the builder's value (the analyzer doesn't; the `watch_field_with_builder` lint catches it), unless the builder names the type (`(bool visible) => …`).

params.name: source
params.doc: The method or field whose value this part shows.

params.name: builder
params.doc: Builds the part for a value: for a text, a [Text] (default: plain `Text(value)`); for states, one widget per value.

params.name: count
params.doc: Number of states of an `int` source (values `0 … count-1`).

params.name: style
params.doc: Style of a text source without [builder].

name: WatchAttributes
summary: HTML attributes of [child]'s element whose values come from a `ThorState` (outside a list; in a list row use `row.attribute`): each method returns the attribute's value, kept current in the browser.
doc:
HTML attributes of [child]'s element whose values come from a
`ThorState` (outside a list; in a list row use `row.attribute`): each
method returns the attribute's value, kept current in the browser.

```dart
WatchAttributes(
  {'aria-rowcount': grid.ariaRowCount},
  child: Semantics(role: SemanticsRole.grid, child: …),
)
```

Names follow `row.attribute`: `aria-*`, `data-*` and a fixed set of
plain attributes, never `on*`, `style` or `class`; a URL attribute with
an unsafe value is left out. Finite states with a different look go
through `Watch(builder:)` instead.

The server writes the first values, so the page is right without JS. An
attribute in [clientOnly] is the exception: the server leaves it out and
the engine writes it when the page starts. Use it for a button that the
state disables (`AttributeName.disabled`) and that must still work
without JS, where nothing would ever enable it again:

```dart
WatchAttributes(
  {AttributeName.disabled: create.invalid},
  clientOnly: {AttributeName.disabled},
  child: FilledButton(buttonType: ButtonType.submit, child: Text('Create')),
)
```

`// web:` no Flutter equivalent (Flutter has no attributes).

constructors.name: WatchAttributes
constructors.summary: Binds each attribute of [attributes] to its method.

params.name: attributes
params.doc: Attribute name → method of a `ThorState` (torn off or with `withArg`) whose result, as text, is the value.

params.name: clientOnly
params.doc: The attributes whose first value the server leaves out: the engine starts the states they name when the page loads (not on the first event, as it does otherwise) and writes them, so without JS the element has none of them.

name: WatchVariables
summary: CSS custom properties of [child]'s element whose values come from a `ThorState`: each method returns a number of pixels, written as `--name: <n>px` and kept current in the browser.
doc:
CSS custom properties of [child]'s element whose values come from a
`ThorState`: each method returns a number of pixels, written as
`--name: <n>px` and kept current in the browser.

```dart
WatchVariables(
  {
    CssVariable<Length>('--grid-before'): grid.spaceBefore,
    CssVariable<Length>('--col-2'): grid.width.withArg(2),
  },
  child: Styled(
    style: StyleProps(
      minHeight: Length.variable(CssVariable('--grid-before')),
    ),
    child: const SizedBox(),
  ),
)
```

For values with no finite set of states (a virtualized list's offset,
a column the user resized): the element's class reads the variable
(`Length.variable`) and only the value changes, so the client still
generates no style. Finite states go through `Watch(builder:)`.

`// web:` no Flutter equivalent (Flutter lays out in Dart). The first
values are in the element's `style`, so the page is right without JS.

This is the low-level layer, with the variable's name in the app's hands
(a stylesheet, a theme or a `StyleProps(raw:)` that reads it). A value a
widget reads (padding, a radius, a size, a position) needs no name:
`BoundLength` (`card.radius.px`) makes the variable, binds it and puts it
on the element that reads it.

constructors.summary: Binds each variable of [variables] to its method.

params.name: variables
params.doc: Variable → method of a `ThorState` returning pixels (`double` or `int`), torn off or with `withArg`.
